# November Photography Itinerary: Peak Autumn Colors

This itinerary focuses on capturing Kyoto's vibrant maples during the peak "Koyo" season. To avoid crowds and capture the best light, early starts are essential.

Day 1: The Golden Temple & Northern Zen
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Kinkakuji_2010-02-14.jpg/1200px-Kinkakuji_2010-02-14.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/camera.svg
- **Kinkaku-ji:** Capture the reflection of the gold leaf against red maples. Best lighting: 09:00 AM.
- **Ryoan-ji:** Minimalist rock garden photography with autumn framing. Best lighting: 11:30 AM.
- **Enko-ji:** Famous for the "framed" view of the garden from the temple interior. Best lighting: 03:30 PM.
Action: [Button: View Map] https://www.google.com/maps/search/temples+northern+kyoto

Day 2: Arashiyama Riverside & Bamboo
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Arashiyama_Bamboo_Grove_Kyoto.jpg/1200px-Arashiyama_Bamboo_Grove_Kyoto.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove:** Soft, filtered light through the stalks. Best lighting: 07:00 AM (to avoid crowds).
- **Tenryu-ji Garden:** Stunning pond reflections of the Sogenchi Garden. Best lighting: 09:30 AM.
- **Okochi Sanso Villa:** Panoramic views of the city and gorge from the tea house. Best lighting: 02:00 PM.
Action: [Button: Arashiyama Guide] https://www.insidekyoto.com/arashiyama-district

Day 3: The Philosophers Path & Illuminations
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/Eikando_Zenrinji_Kyoto05n.jpg/1200px-Eikando_Zenrinji_Kyoto05n.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- **Nanzen-ji:** Large brick aqueduct set against fiery maples. Best lighting: 10:00 AM.
- **Eikan-do:** Widely considered the best foliage spot in Kyoto. Best lighting: 03:00 PM.
- **Kodai-ji Night Illumination:** Capturing the high-contrast light shows on the trees. Best lighting: 06:00 PM.
Action: [Button: Check Illuminations] https://www.kyototourism.org/en/column/13444/

Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Tofuku-ji_Tsuten-kyo_01.jpg/1200px-Tofuku-ji_Tsuten-kyo_01.jpg Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

- **Bishamon-do:** Famous for the "red carpet" of fallen maple leaves on the steps. Best lighting: 04:30 PM.

# Gion Tea Culture & Seafood-Free Dining

In Japan, "Dashi" (fish stock) is ubiquitous. To ensure a strict no-seafood/no-dashi diet, these recommendations focus on **Shojin Ryori** (Buddhist vegan cuisine) and dedicated vegan restaurants.

**Authentic Tea Ceremony: Camellia Flower Teahouse**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
Located in a quiet lane in Gion, Camellia provides a professional, English-guided ceremony. You will learn the history of Zen and tea while whisking your own matcha.
Action: [Button: Book Camellia] https://www.tea-kyoto.com/

**Safe Dining Options (No Seafood/No Dashi)**
1. **Shigetsu (Arashiyama):** Located inside Tenryu-ji Temple. Authentic Shojin Ryori (Buddhist vegan) served in a stunning garden setting.
2. **Towzen (Sakyo-ku):** Famous for Vegan Ramen. The broth is creamy soy-milk based, completely free of animal or fish products.
3. **Mumokuteki Cafe (Central):** A trendy plant-based cafe that avoids all seafood and dashi. Great for lunch near the shopping arcades.
4. **Ain Soph Journey (Kawaramachi):** A fully vegan restaurant specializing in "Heavenly Pancakes" and savory meals with no fish stock.
5. **Veg Out (Near Kyoto Station):** Riverside vegan cafe offering macrobiotic bowls and sandwiches, ideal for a safe, seafood-free breakfast or lunch.
